parallel_lanes_not_duplicated: Trigger-4 WP1201 source implementation and CI

observed_wp1201_strengths: fixed allow-list rather than arbitrary caller-supplied probes
read-only bounded command/file probes with per-probe timeout/error handling
UNKNOWN is explicit and cannot contain a value
missing XDG runtime ownership remains UNKNOWN rather than inferred
deterministic canonical JSON SHA-256 snapshot digest
baseline probe set avoids raw machine-id, serial-number fields, MAC addresses, credentials, clipboard, user documents and raw camera/microphone payloads

observed_architecture_gaps.finding: profile_digest_sha256 hashes the entire fact map, mixing comparatively stable platform facts with volatile session/device/software/runtime facts. Any one fact change therefore changes the one global profile digest and can unnecessarily stale unrelated evidence if downstream consumers bind only that digest.

WP1201 provides a snapshot digest but no separate stable pseudonymous host-scope identity. External systemd evidence shows raw machine-id must not be exposed and also does not track hardware replacement, so stable lineage and mutable current-host profile need separate identities.
The profile lacks a distinct boot-scope identity. Reboot-sensitive lifecycle/readback evidence therefore needs an independent boot epoch rather than using whole-profile digest changes as a proxy.

The audio probe stores raw `wpctl status` output in the fingerprint. This is operationally useful but is a dynamic runtime topology surface and should not automatically participate in every host-evidence binding; it may also include transient application/media stream descriptions beyond a minimal platform fingerprint.

The current schema exposes one complete_fingerprint boolean and one global digest. Completion maturity, however, is requirement-specific: evidence for storage migration, audio, camera, desktop session and service lifecycle should invalidate on different subsets of host state.

external_primary_constraints.machine_id_rule: raw machine-id is confidential; use an application-specific irreversible derived identifier for untrusted/exported contexts
external_primary_constraints.identity_scope_rule: machine, boot, service invocation and login/session are separate identity scopes
external_primary_constraints.machine_id_hardware_rule: machine-id remains stable when hardware is replaced, so it cannot be the current hardware fingerprint

recommended_successor_architecture.preserve_wp1201_g1: YES_AS_COARSE_SNAPSHOT_COMPONENT; do not rewrite or revoke its repository-CI acceptance
new_typed_scopes: HostScopeIdentity: application-specific pseudonymous stable host/install lineage; raw machine-id never stored/exported
BootScopeIdentity: boot-epoch identity kept separate from host lineage
HostProfileComponent: independently canonicalized/digested components such as platform, software/kernel, session, device, audio, browser/adapter
HostRuntimeWitness: volatile current-state observations such as media streams/service state that are not stable fingerprint material
RequirementBindingDigest: deterministic digest over only the exact component IDs/digests required by a specific acceptance obligation
recommended_successor_architecture.whole_snapshot_digest: May remain for snapshot provenance, but CompletionGate and evidence reuse should bind requirement-specific component digests rather than treating every host change as globally invalidating.
recommended_successor_architecture.privacy_rule: Prefer parsed minimal structured fields over retaining broad command output. Volatile application/media stream names should be excluded from the stable host profile unless an explicit requirement needs them.
recommended_successor_architecture.unknown_rule: UNKNOWN remains component-local and contributes unknown debt only to obligations that require that component; an unknown browser probe must not by itself block unrelated storage or state-migration acceptance.
recommended_successor_architecture.twin_rule: All simulated/twin profiles carry explicit backend/fidelity identity and remain capped at SIMULATED_HOST_VERIFIED; no derived host scope ID or matching software profile can mint physical EXACT_HOST_BOUND credit.

counterhypothesis: A single monolithic digest is simpler and maximally conservative: any host change invalidates all host-bound evidence, avoiding accidental reuse. This may be preferable if host probes are rare and revalidation is cheap. The successor split is justified only if measured false-staleness/revalidation cost is material without weakening safety.
falsifier: Build a no-source-edit fixture around WP1201 outputs and compare monolithic versus component/requirement binding across controlled deltas: audio stream start/stop, browser update, USB hotplug, reboot, kernel update, permission loss and synthetic platform change. A valid split must preserve rejection for requirement-relevant changes while reducing invalidation for irrelevant changes; otherwise retain the monolithic model.

trigger4_handoff.suggested_successor: WP1201 generation-2 or adjacent host-evidence binding workpackage after current reconciliation
tests: raw machine-id never appears in persisted/exported profile or receipt
same host + new audio stream leaves non-audio requirement binding unchanged
reboot changes BootScopeIdentity and invalidates reboot-sensitive evidence
USB change invalidates device-requiring obligations but not unrelated state-migration evidence
kernel/driver change invalidates requirements that bind kernel/driver component
host-scope identity remains stable across benign profile changes but is never treated as proof of unchanged hardware

efficiency_effect.expected_benefit: less false-stale evidence and less unnecessary physical revalidation while preserving fail-closed requirement-specific invalidation
efficiency_effect.runtime_cost: small additional canonical hashes over already collected structured facts
efficiency_effect.token_context_cost: lower if downstream context selects only required components instead of full raw profile output
efficiency_effect.privacy_effect: improved by separating volatile/runtime observation from stable profile and parsing broad command outputs
